rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted reading is لقوا; a variant لاقوا has the same sense, but recitation must follow what is widely transmitted from the Prophet and Companions.
rows.anchor: ظاهر القراءة لقوا وعن بعضهم لاقوا والمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Meeting is the opposite of being screened; fundamentally it is two things encountering one another face to face.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: كل شيء استقبل شيئا وصادفه فقد لقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلا is the opposite of being among others; mockery and derision are synonyms of jest, while seriousness is their opposite.
rows.anchor: والهزء والسخرية بمعنى، ونظيره الهزل، ونقيضه الجد.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He defines Satan as any rebellious being among jinn, humans, or animals; another lexicographer defines one as rebellious from any species.
rows.anchor: الشيطان: كل عات متمرد من الجن والإنس والدواب، عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two etymologies are offered: Satan may be distant from good (form fayʿāl) or associated with burning (form faʿlān); the verb means becoming satan-like.
rows.anchor: وأصله من. شطن إذا بعد، كأنه بعد عن الخير، ووزنه فيعال، وقيل: هو من الشيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لقوا derives from لقيوا, with the vowel moved and adjacent silent letters resolved by deleting the wāw.
rows.anchor: لقوا أصله: لقيوا فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء، فنقلت إلى القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلى may mean ‘with,’ as in 3:52 and an Arabic proverb, or mark a destination; here it marks turning from believers to leaders.
rows.anchor: قيل: الذود إلى الذود إبل، عن النضر بن شميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلوت به can mean mocking someone or being alone with him, whereas خلوت إليه indicates making him the destination of one's need.
rows.anchor: ويقال: خلوت به يحتمل معنيين هزئت به وسخرت، وانفردت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا contracts إننا by deleting the second nūn to avoid a doubled consonant; the full form also occurs in Qur'anic usage.
rows.anchor: والأصل في إنا: إننا، حذفت النون استثقالا للتضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the hypocrites said they would remain well as long as the other party lived, the Muslims reported what happened to the Messenger, and God revealed this verse.
rows.anchor: بما جرى فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites professed belief in what was revealed to Muhammad when they met believers in order to protect their lives and property.
rows.anchor: يعني المنافقين إذا رأوا المؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘Their satans’ means their leaders among disbelievers; al-Jishumī prefers this over jinn because most scholars hold it, it is more natural, and the context excludes soothsayers. Al-Kalbi reports jinn satans.
rows.anchor: قيل: رؤسائهم من الكفار، عن ابن عباس، وقيل: شياطين الجن، عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report identifies their leaders as five Jews, including Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and Abu Burda.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم خمسة نفر من اليهود: كعب بن الأشرف بالمدينة، وأبو بردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We are with you’ means either that they share their leaders' religion or that they are their supporters.
rows.anchor: أي على دينكم، وقيل: أنصاركم.

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: One proposed motive was winning over their leaders; another was mocking the believers and Muhammad's companions by professing faith.
rows.anchor: قيل: استمالتهم لرؤسائهم، عن أبي علي، وقيل: استهزاء بالمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns religious hypocrisy and ostentation, mockery of people of truth, and the grave offense of siding with unbelievers.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على قبح النفاق في الدين، والتحذير من ذلك، وكذلك الرياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has plural wāw and singular ‘trade’; reported variants alter the wāw's vowel or pluralize trade, but are rejected for lacking widespread transmission; fatḥ on wāw can be confused with dual marking.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: اشتروا بضم الواو، وتجارتهم على الواحد، وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buying fundamentally means exchange: اشترى commonly means bought and شرى sold, although اشتريت can also mean sold; a sale is an exchange contract with legal conditions.
rows.anchor: أصل الشراء: الاستبدال، يقال: اشترى إذا ابتاع، وشرى إذا باع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Profit is the increase over capital, and trade is pursuing profit through sale; تجار is the plural of تاجر.
rows.anchor: والربح: الزيادة على رأس المال، ربح يربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance originally means destruction and can mean leading from religion, judging someone astray, or losing the way to reward and Paradise; attributing misguidance to God is figurative except leading from religion, which is morally wrong.
rows.anchor: والضلال: أصله الهلاك، ثم يستعمل في معان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural wāw takes ḍamma after two silent letters because it signals plurality; لو استطعنا instead keeps the basic linking vowel.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الواو من علامة الجمع كان الضم أدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in ‘their trade did not profit’ reflects an implied conditional: if they exchanged guidance for error, their trade did not profit.
rows.anchor: لأن في الكلام معنى الجزاء وجوابه، كأنه قال: إذا اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes hypocrites as exchanging disbelief for faith; the author surveys seven explanations for how this applies if they never possessed guidance.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما هم عليه من الضلالة والخسران، فقال: أولئك يعني المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes ‘bought’ to mean chose and preferred, though this is not the apparent Arabic meaning.
rows.anchor: أن المراد ب اشتروا اختاروا واستحبوا؛ لأن كل مشتر مختار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they believed and then disbelieved; the author rejects this as unsupported diversion from the wording and inconsistent with the passage.
rows.anchor: أنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا، فهو عموم أريد به الخصوص، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The preferred view is that they abandoned faith for disbelief; it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Abu ʿAli, and others.
rows.anchor: تركوا الإيمان إلى الكفر، واستبدلوه به، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may have exchanged their innate disposition for disbelief, as described in a prophetic report.
rows.anchor: أنهم ولدوا على الفطرة كما جاء في الخبر، فتركوا ذلك إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Before Muhammad's mission they believed in and foretold him; when he was sent, they rejected him and replaced that faith with disbelief.
rows.anchor: استبدلوا بالإيمان الذي كانوا عليه قبل البعثة؛ لأنهم كانوا يؤمنون بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because disbelievers can choose either faith or disbelief, choosing disbelief is like exchanging faith for it.
rows.anchor: لما كان الكافر متمكنا منهما فاختار الكفر على الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that they professed faith outwardly and abandoned it inwardly.
rows.anchor: أنهم آمنوا ظاهرا، ثم تركوا الإيمان باطنا

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand the exchange as disbelief for faith; Abu Muslim instead reads it as choosing punishment and destruction over guidance, Paradise, and reward.
rows.anchor: فقيل: الكفر بالإيمان، عن أكثر المفسرين، وقيل: اشتروا: اختاروا العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Their trade did not profit’ means they gained no benefit from their exchange.
rows.anchor: تجارتهم) أي لم ينتفعوا بذلك

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Misguidance here means being destroyed or lost at the divine proof; only unbelieving sinners perish through it, or only sinners are misled by it.
rows.anchor: يعني: ضلوا عنده، عن الأصم وأبي مسلم، والضلال في الأصل هو الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner is one who leaves obedience to God for disobedience and divine friendship for enmity.
rows.anchor: والفاسق من خرج من طاعة الله إلى معصيته، ومن ولايته إلى عداوته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the ‘people of innate knowledge’: believers are praised for knowledge and distinguished from unbelievers, so they cannot all have equal knowledge.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على إبطال قول أصحاب المعارف؛ لأنه تعالى مدح المؤمن بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling فسق a sin is revealed legal usage because it is used as reproach; the verse also entails certain punishment of sinners, against the Murjiʾa.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين) على أن الفسق اسم شرعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance from God can be punishment, and proofs may be explained subtly or plainly to achieve their purpose.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الضلال من الله يكون عقابا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misleads only sinners, not believers too as the Compulsionists claim; this leads into the covenant-breakers of 2:27.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يضل إلا الفاسق، خلاف قول المجبرة: إنه يضل المؤمن أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking undoes what was firmly joined, opposite to binding or sound construction; metaphorically it invalidates a doctrine or proof.
rows.anchor: النقض والهدم والكسر نظائر، وهو إفساد ما أبرمت، ونقيضه الإبرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Covenant can mean a command, testament, or binding pact; covenant, compact, and bond share the sense of firmness.
rows.anchor: والعهد: الأمر، والعهد: الوصية، والعهد: الموثق، والجمع: عهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every morally responsible person receives God's covenant through rational proofs of the Creator and Benefactor and through commands and prohibitions delivered by messengers.
rows.anchor: وكل مكلف فقد أخذ الله عليه الميثاق بشيئين: بما ركب في عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting is the opposite of joining; the doubled form can indicate repeated or emphatic cutting, while joining means combining or attaching.
rows.anchor: والقطع: نقيض الوصل، ونظيره الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commands may express obligation, recommendation, permission, threat, challenge, or creation; their basic meaning is a request, and most scholars say they imply obligation.
rows.anchor: والأصل في الجميع الطلب، وحقيقة الأمر في القول

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
rows.claim: They hold that commands indicate recommendation, unlike the majority view of obligation; the author rejects suspending judgment as untenable.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على الندب، عن أبي علي وأبي هاشم، وقيل: على التوقف، وليس بشيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss is the opposite of profit and fundamentally means losing one's capital.
rows.anchor: والخسران: نقيض الربح، خسر خسرانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين is accusative as an adjective qualifying the sinful, or nominative as a condemnatory clause whose predicate is ‘those are the losers.’
rows.anchor: نصب؛ لأنه صفة للفاسقين، ويصلح الرفع على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من after ‘after’ may be an extra particle or mark the starting point of breaking; أن يوصل may be genitive as a substitute or accusative as an object.
rows.anchor: قيل: صلة وزيادة، وقيل: معناها ابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: God's covenant may be rational evidence, the prophetic promise concerning Muhammad recorded in earlier scriptures, or God's commands and prohibitions; the latter is reported from Abu Muslim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما قدم إليهم على ألسن الرسل من صفة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that this is the covenant taken from Adam's descendants is rejected because people do not remember it and there is no evidence, so it cannot establish an obligation.
rows.anchor: فأما من قال: إنه العهد الذي أخذه الله تعالى على ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described may be Jewish scholars, including hypocrites, or all unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قيل: أحبار اليهود، ومنهم المنافقون، وقيل: جميع الكفار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘after its covenant’ may refer to God, who confirmed it, or to the covenant itself; both readings are acceptable.
rows.anchor: قيل: تعود على اسم الله تعالى، يعني أنه وكده عليهم، وقيل: ترجع على الميثاق

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Breaking what God ordered joined may mean severing kinship with the Messenger from enmity and envy; reports also mention the Prophet and believers, kinship ties, or belief in all prophets and scriptures, and the author allows the broad sense to cover all.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قطعوا رحم رسول الله بعداوته بغضا وحسدا، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption means inviting others to disbelief, practicing disbelief, or resulting insecurity, banditry, and injustice that faith would prevent.
rows.anchor: قيل: استدعاؤهم إلى الكفر هو الفساد، وقيل: عملهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Losers have ruined themselves like those who lose their capital; alternatively they miss Paradise and deserve the Fire.
rows.anchor: أولئك هم الخاسرون أي أهلكوا أنفسهم فهم بمنزلة من هلك رأس ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ and murābaṭa share a root sense of tying; military ribāṭ means remaining at a frontier to repel enemy harm, like tethering horses, while muṣābara is mutual steadfastness.
rows.anchor: الرباط والمرابطة واحد، وأصل الربط الشد، ربطت الشيء أربطه ربطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands follow the account of believers and unbelievers to urge obedience, religious commitment, and jihad; alternatively believers should emulate those who fought and died and their reward.
rows.anchor: لما حكى تعالى أحوال المؤمنين والكافرين فيما تقدم حث على الصبر على الطاعة

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك
rows.claim: They interpret the sequence as patience in obeying God, steadfastness against God's enemies in jihad, and guarding the frontier for God's cause.
rows.anchor: اصبروا على طاعة الله وصابروا أعداء الله في الجهاد ورابطوا في سبيل الله عن الحسن

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: He interprets it as steadfastness in religion, mutual competition in response to God's promises, and standing against enemies.
rows.anchor: اصبروا على دينكم، وصابروا وعدي إياكم، ورابطوا أعداءكم عن محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: He reads the commands as patience in jihad, endurance against the enemy, and tethering horses for battle.
rows.anchor: اصبروا على الجهاد، وصابروا العدو، ورابطوا الخيل عليه عن زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: He interprets ribāṭ as waiting for one prayer after another.
rows.anchor: ورابطوا بانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success may mean attaining the desired reward, avoiding the nullification of good deeds, or doing these acts in hope of success.
rows.anchor: لعلكم تفلحون يعني لتفلحوا؛ أي لتنالوا البغية من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands cover duty: worship and avoiding sin, opposing adversaries by hand and tongue, defending Islam at frontiers, and avoiding all wrongdoing; success depends on such acts, against the Murjiʾa.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على جماع ما يتناوله التكليف؛ لأن قوله: اصبروا يتناول العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has rushd with ḍamma then sukūn; al-Sulamī reads both vowels open. They are two forms of a word meaning right guidance rather than error.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة رشدا بضم الراء وسكون الشين، وقرأ السلمي بفتحهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ابتلاء means testing; nikāḥ can denote the marriage contract or intercourse; īnās is perceiving, seeing, hearing, or knowing, originally sensing what is familiar.
rows.anchor: الابتلاء: الاختبار، ابتلى يبتلي ابتلاء، والنكاح يعبر به عن العقد وعن الوطء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isrāf is exceeding limits; badār is haste; ʿiffa is refraining from what is unlawful.
rows.anchor: والإسراف: مجاوزة الحد، ومنه السرف تجاوز الحد في التقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إسرافا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative, object, or cognate accusative; بدارا is also a cognate accusative, warning against hastening before the orphan grows up.
rows.anchor: إسرافا نصب على الحال، وقيل: لأنه مفعول، وقيل: نصب على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Thabit ibn Rifaʿa and his uncle: after Thabit's father died leaving a child, the uncle asked the Prophet what he could take and when to return the property.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في ثابت بن رفاعة وفي عمه، وذلك أن رفاعة توفي وترك ابنه وهو صغير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: The guardian, executor, judge, or trusted agent should test orphans' intellect and capacity to manage their property.
rows.anchor: أي اختبروا وجربوا عقولهم وصلاحهم لمالهم عن ابن عباس والسدي

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say guardians must test both reason and religion because frivolous conduct can lead an orphan to squander property.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اختبروا عقولهم ودينهم عن الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Until they reach marriage’ may mean puberty, as Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd say, or reaching the age when marriage is needed and adulthood begins.
rows.anchor: قيل: الحلم عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد، وتقديره: حتى إذا بلغوا حال النكاح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘If you perceive sound judgment’ may mean you recognize it; the first of three views defines it as soundness of reason and religion.
rows.anchor: قيل: عرفتم عن ابن عباس، وقيل: أبصرتم منهم من اليتامى رشدا فيه ثلاثة أقوال

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads ‘the abode of the Hereafter’ with one lām by annexation; the other readers use two lām letters and make ‘Hereafter’ an adjective.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر: ولدار الآخرة مضافا بلام واحدة لاختلاف اللفظين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ between addressing the audience and speaking of absent people in ‘will you not understand?’ across this verse and the cited occurrences in al-Aʿrāf, Yusuf, Yunus, and Ya-Sin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر ويعقوب: أفلا تعقلون بالتاء ههنا وفي سورة (الأعراف)

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: To taste means to test or experience; al-Khalil says anything painful that befalls a person has been tasted.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: [كل ما] نزل بإنسان من مكروه فقد ذاقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss means diminution or destruction; its central idea is decrease, though some say its origin is destruction.
rows.anchor: وأصل الباب: النقصان، وقيل: أصله الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting primarily means encountering or facing someone, then by extension seeing; it can also mean living in the same era or encountering calamity and battle without literal sight.
rows.anchor: وكل شيء صادف شيئا، أو استقبله فقد لقيه، تقول: لقيت فلانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtatan means sudden arrival without the person knowing when it will occur.
rows.anchor: والبغتة: الفجأة، وهو ورود الشيء على [صاحبه بغير] علمه بوقته

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers lighten the nūn in a-taḥājjūnī by deleting one of two nūns; other readers assimilate them and read a doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر: أتحاجوني خفيفة النون على حذف إحدى النونين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: They retain the yāʾ in هداني, while other readers omit it for ease because context supplies it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: هداني بإثبات الياء على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥājja is each disputant's demand for proof and presentation of evidence; guidance is direction leading to truth, and sulṭān means proof or power enabling control.
rows.anchor: المحاجة: طلب كل واحد من الخصمين الحجة، وإيراد كل واحد الحجة على صاحبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Security is calmness of the soul; īmān is associated with security from punishment through one's deeds.
rows.anchor: والأمن: سكون النفس، ومنه: الأمان والإيمان؛ لأنه عمل ما يؤمن العقاب معه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception in ‘unless my Lord wills’ may be disconnected, meaning ‘but I fear my Lord's reproach,’ or literal: idols could be given power or restored by God's will.
rows.anchor: قيل: نصب على تقدير: لكن أخاف مسبة ربي، و(إلا) ههنا بمعنى: (لكن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's ‘how should I fear?’ is a denial: powerless idols cannot benefit or harm, and the question challenges people for fearing them while worshipping without proof.
rows.anchor: والمراد الإنكار؛ أي لا ينبغي أن أخاف ما لا ينفع ولا يضر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of ‘We raise’ varies between nun plus genitive annexation, nun with accusative indefinite ‘degrees,’ and Yaʿqub's yāʾ form at the parallel Yusuf passage.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو: (نرفع) بالنون (درجات من نشاء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith means affirmation linguistically; in religious usage it names performing obligations and avoiding major sins. Lubs means mixing; proof is evidence relied on for a claim.
rows.anchor: الإيمان: هو التصديق في اللغة، وفي الشرع: اسم لأداء الواجبات

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وابن إسحاق وأبو علي
rows.claim: ‘Those who believe’ may be God's own answer, settling the dispute between Abraham and his people by declaring which party is secure.
rows.anchor: قيل: من الله على جهة فصل القضاء بذلك بين إبراهيم وقومه، عن ابن زيد وابن إسحاق وأبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham's people answer his question about which group deserves security, giving evidence against themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جواب قومه لما سألهم: أي الفريقين أحق بالأمن؟

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another view makes Abraham answer his own question; the author also treats this as continuation of Abraham's argument for unity, justice, promise, and warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جواب إبراهيم كما يسأل العالم ويجيب نفسه، حكاه الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: ‘They did not mix faith with wrongdoing’ means they did not commit shirk, identified as great wrongdoing in 31:13; a prophetic report reassured Companions troubled by the verse.
rows.anchor: قيل: بشرك، عن ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وأبي بكر وحذيفة وسلمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes harm to oneself or others and major sins, not minor sins expiated by obedience or repentance; the garment metaphor also suggests a grave sin affecting deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد ظلم نفسه وظلم غيره، والمراد به الكبائر دون الصغائر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Security is safety from punishment on Judgment Day; guidance means Paradise or truth and religion.
rows.anchor: أولئك لهم الأمن يعني المستبصر في الدين آمن يوم القيامة من العذاب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: God gave Abraham the proof as He gave the Prophet proof; alternatively, He brought it to mind or instructed and prompted Abraham to use it.
rows.anchor: قيل: كما أعطيناك الحجة أعطيناها إبراهيم، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account of Abraham's proof is that worship belongs only to the powerful, eternal, all-knowing owner of benefit and harm.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يعبد من لا ينفع ولا يضر، وإنما المستحق للعبادة مالك النفع والضر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Other arguments ask whether one God or many gods deserves security, and turn the people's fear of idols back on their worship of small and great beings.
rows.anchor: أي الفريقين أحق بالأمن: من يعبد إلها واحدا، أو من يعبد آلهة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God left people unforced for moral responsibility and testing, so they must follow evidence rather than caprice; imitation, habit, doubt, neglect of inquiry, and worldly motives lead to ruin.
rows.anchor: والامتحان، وتدل على أن الواجب اتباع الدليل فقط، دون اتباع الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿālaw means ‘come near’; the word comes from elevation, as if the caller speaks from a high place.
rows.anchor: معنى تعال: أقبل وادن، وأصله: من العلو والارتفاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥrīm fundamentally means preventing or forbidding; it is related to ḥajr and ḥaẓr and opposed to release or permission.
rows.anchor: والتحريم: أصله المنع، ونظيره: الحجر والحظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation is distinct from the recited original speech, just as a retelling differs from what is retold; it can mean reading or repeating a narration.
rows.anchor: والتلاوة: القراءة، والتلاوة غير المتلو كما أن الحكاية غير المحكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imlāq means poverty or having no provisions; the related words for flattery suggest a poor person striving to draw near for gain.
rows.anchor: والإملاق: الإفلاس من المال والزاد، وهو الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawāḥish are deeds greatly foul, and waṣṣā and awṣā both mean enjoining or charging someone with an instruction.
rows.anchor: والفواحش: جمع فاحشة، وهو: القبيح العظيم في القبح، ووصى وأوصى بمعنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may be the object of ‘recite,’ meaning what was forbidden, or the object of ‘forbid,’ meaning ‘what thing did your Lord forbid?’
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان: الأول: نصب ب (أتل) أي: أتل الذي حرم عليكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial alif of أتلو is omitted because the jussive particle's deletion rule found no added letter to remove.
rows.anchor: قلنا: لأن الجازم لما كان عمله الحذف فلم يصادف زيادة عمل في النفس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: ألا تشركوا may be nominative, accusative under ‘enjoined,’ ‘recite,’ or ‘forbade,’ a substitute, an exhortation, or a free-standing prohibition; تشركوا may be subjunctive under أن or jussive under لا.
rows.anchor: موضع (أن) فيه ثلاثة أقوال: الأول: الرفع على تقدير: ذلك ألا تشركوا به شيئا.

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: The prohibition of shirk and command to avoid it are equivalent; forbidding shirk states the same rule as commanding that it not be done.
rows.anchor: لا فرق بين قوله: حرم ربكم عليكم، وبين قوله: أمر ألا تفعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the text pairs prohibitions with corresponding duties, details what is recited rather than what is forbidden, or uses an exhortation construction.
rows.anchor: فمما حرم فعله الشرك، وأوجب ألا تشركوا، وحرم العقوق، وأوجب الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse prohibits worshipping or claiming divinity for anything alongside God and commands kindness to parents, whose care follows God's in nurturing people.
rows.anchor: يعني في العبادة وادعاء الإلهية وبالوالدين إحسانا يعني أمركم بالإحسان إلى الوالدين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن جريج والضحاك
rows.claim: ‘Do not kill your children from poverty’ addresses killing children, including burying daughters alive for fear of hardship; God provides for parents and children.
rows.anchor: قيل: من الفقر، عن ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن جريج والضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Indecencies can include all sins or adultery; the author favors a broad ban on major sins, publicly and privately. Reports distinguish outward and inward acts and what is visible or hidden.
rows.anchor: قيل: المعاصي والقبائح كلها، وقيل: الزنا، وقيل: يدخل الصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: The public/hidden distinction forbids secret adultery, which some people did not consider wrong; another report says it corrects a false assumption about private conduct.
rows.anchor: قيل: لأنهم كانوا لا يرون بالزنا سرا بأسا فنهى عن ذلك، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: One gloss makes public indecency wine and hidden indecency adultery.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما ظهر الخمر، وما بطن الزنا عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Public and hidden indecencies may mean deeds visible to people and deeds concealed from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو ما ظهر للناس وما هو باطن عنهم، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on killing a protected person is repeated despite being included among indecencies to emphasize its gravity; protected lives include believers and treaty partners.
rows.anchor: تفخيما لشأنه، وتعظيما لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Except by right’ allows killing for apostasy, adultery by a married person, unjust murder, rebellion against a just imam, highway robbery, or in self-defense.
rows.anchor: وهو الردة والزنا إذا كان محصنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded these matters so people would learn and comply, recognize His mercy, and use reason to identify their duties.
rows.anchor: أي: تعلمون ذلك فامتثلوا أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception to the prohibition on killing is general and needs specification; the Prophet explains it as apostasy after faith, adultery after chastity, and unjust killing.
rows.anchor: الاستثناء مجملا كان المستثنى منه أيضا مجملا فيحتاج إلى بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These acts are human acts subject to reward and punishment, against the Compulsionists' account of created acts.
rows.anchor: وتدل أن هذه الأشياء فعلهم؛ لذلك تعلق به الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read tadhakkarūn without doubling the dhāl; other readers double it throughout the Qur'an, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم تذكرون بالتخفيف، وقرأ الباقون تذكرون

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Al-ashudd may be a plural of shiddah; other grammarians say it has no singular or is itself singular. It means a youth's developed strength, as in ʿAntara's line.
rows.anchor: الأشد: قال علي بن عيسى جمع شد، كما أن الأصر جمع صر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim parses al-ashudd as the plural of shiddah, like niʿmah/anʿum; qist means justice.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: الأشد جمع شدة مثل نعمة وأنعم

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: A line attributed through al-Mufaḍḍal uses شد النهار for the height or strength of daylight as evidence for al-ashudd.
rows.anchor: قال عنترة: رواه المفضل: عهدي به شد النهار كأنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذا قربى is the predicate of kāna with its subject omitted; awfaw and waffaw have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: نصب ذا قربى على خبر (كان)، واسم (كان) محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan is a child without a father; the verse says not to approach the child's property except beneficially, emphasizing caution because the child cannot defend self or property.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربوا يعني لا تتأولوا ولا تأخذوا، وإنما ذكر القرب تأكيدا

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: ‘In the best manner’ can mean protecting the property until maturity or investing it through trade; other views allow customary guardian consumption, borrowing, or use of an animal or servant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي حفظه إلى أن يكبر فيسلم المال إليه، وقيل: ينميه بالتجارة

rows.speaker: أبو علي وابن زيد
rows.claim: A guardian may consume from the orphan's property according to custom, but this view excludes clothing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أكل القيم عليه بالمعروف دون الكسوة، عن أبي علي وابن زيد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-ashudd may mean thirty years; other reports give puberty, maturity around eighteen to thirty, or full strength.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يحتلم فتكتب عليه الحسنات والسيئات عن يحيى بن [يعمر والشعبي]

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa sets al-ashudd at twenty-five; the judge instead selects when a youth can protect the property, which the author says reflects the purpose of the limit.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حنيفة، وقيل: حتى يتقوى على حفظ [ماله]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching full strength alone does not require handing over property; the implied condition is that sound judgment also be evident so the orphan can preserve it.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية حذف؛ لأن مجرد بلوغ الأشد لا يوجب دفع ماله إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The capacity clause excuses unavoidable tiny errors in measure or weight; another gloss is that God assigns only what is manageable and lawful.
rows.anchor: قيل: في إيفاء الكيل والوزن، حتى لا يؤاخذ في ذلك بالحبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘When you speak, be just’ requires truth in testimony, speech, wills, enjoining right, legal opinions, judgments, rulings, and schools of thought.
rows.anchor: وهذا من الأوامر العجيبة البليغة التي يعقل فيها مع قلة حروفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the person judged or testified about is a relative, kinship must not prevent truthful speech.
rows.anchor: فلا تمنعن قرابته أن تقولوا الصدق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God's covenant includes obligations, the commands in these verses, oaths, and what one binds oneself to; the author says all are intended, while Ibn ʿAbbas calls these rulings clear and unabrogated.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخ منها شيء

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says these verses open the Torah; al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym compares them to a page bearing Muhammad's seal.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب: أول التوراة هذه الآيات، وعن الربيع بن خثيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing purpose may be remembering, taking admonition, avoiding neglect, reflecting on duties, recalling punishment, or becoming people of remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كي لا تغفلوا عنه، وتتركوا العمل به، وقيل:

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Yaʿqub read وإن with light kasra and silent nūn; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī double the nūn; other readers use أن with fatḥa and doubling.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب وإن هذا بكسر ألف أن وسكون النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in the vowel of the yāʾ in ṣirāṭī and in saying ṣirāṭī or sirāṭī; these are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: والقراء أجمعوا على سكون الياء من صراطي غير ابن عامر فإنه فتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, the clause can attach to the preceding prohibition or mean ‘because this is My path’; with kasra, it can continue ‘recite’ or begin a new sentence.
rows.anchor: فأما فتح (إن) ففيه وجهان: الأول: العطف على ألا تشركوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirāṭ means road; religious law is a road to Paradise, whereas Satan's way leads to Hell.
rows.anchor: الصراط: الطريق، وإنما قيل للشرع طريق؛ لأنه يؤدي إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative mustaqīman highlights that the path is straight as well as a path; it is parsed as a circumstantial phrase or specification.
rows.anchor: إنما الفائدة في اجتماع أنه صراط، وأنه مستقيم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: God's straight path is Islam; another gloss is the Qur'an and proofs, without crookedness or contradiction.
rows.anchor: أي: الإسلام طريقي الذي أمرت بها، وقيل: القرآن وسائر الحجج

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The forbidden divergent paths are religions opposed to Islam or paths of disbelief; following the true way means practicing and affirming it and observing its lawful and forbidden parts.
rows.anchor: فاتبعوه أي: اقتدوا به واعملوا به، واعتقدوا صحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the true path divides people and destroys unity; God's charge may refer to the Qur'an, Islam, preceding commands, avoiding sins, or avoiding punishment through obedience.
rows.anchor: فتفرق بكم عن سبيله يعني إذا تركتم طريق الحق المستقيم تفرقتم

rows.speaker: عاصم عن حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads ā-mantum with one hamza as a statement; Abu Bakr, Hamza, and al-Kisāʾī use two hamzas, while most readers use one lengthened hamza as a question.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم في رواية حفص قال فرعون آمنتم بهمزة واحدة على لفظ الخبر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The common reading has tanqimū with kasra on the qāf; al-Hasan uses fatḥa, and both forms express taking vengeance or punishing.
rows.anchor: وظاهر القراءة ما تنقم بكسر القاف، وعن الحسن بفتحها، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqṭīʿ means multiplying cuts; ṣalb is binding to wood, and inqilāb is returning, derived from turning back.
rows.anchor: نظيره: التفصيل والتفريق، ونقيضه: التوصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pouring patience is likened to emptying a vessel; patience is holding oneself through hardship. God should not be called ‘patient’; Abu ʿAli rejects al-Ṣabūr unless a report is sound, then explains it as forbearance.
rows.anchor: وأفرغ علينا صبرا شبه بحال إفراغ الإناء كما يقال: صب عليه صبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا is contracted from إننا by deleting one nūn; Rabbana is parsed as a vocative with annexation.
rows.anchor: أصل (إنا) (إننا)، فإذا قيل: (إننا)، فقد ورد على أصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supporting Muslims is alike publicly or secretly, through speech, fighting, or financial aid; repentance is accepted from every unbeliever, and support, allegiance, repentance, and piety are human acts.
rows.anchor: بالمال؛ لأن جميع ذلك مظاهرة على المسلمين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insilākh means removing something from its covering, like skinning a sheep or a snake leaving its skin; a month is said to shed when it ends.
rows.anchor: الانسلاح: إخراج الشيء عما لا يشبهه، وكذلك سلخ الشاة نزع جلدها

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ḥaṣr can mean sickness or restraint, while ḥaṣara can mean an enemy's siege; Ibn al-Sikkit distinguishes them, and the author says the first distinction is correct.
rows.anchor: والحصر: المرض والمنع، أحصره المرض وحصره، وحصره العدو، قاله ابن السكيت

rows.speaker: عامر بن الطفيل وعدي بن زيد
rows.claim: Marṣad, lookout, and observation post are near-synonyms; Amir ibn al-Tufayl and ʿAdi ibn Zayd use marṣad for where death waits.
rows.anchor: والمرصد والمربأ والمرقب نظائر، رصده يرصده رصدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijāra is seeking protection or a protector; granting protection makes the seeker safe, as if taking the person into one's neighborhood.
rows.anchor: والاستجارة: طلب الجور أو المجير، والجار والمستجير بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلاغ and إيصال both mean conveying to an endpoint; reaching a term may mean approaching its end rather than passing it.
rows.anchor: والإبلاغ والإيصال من النظائر، والإبلاغ: التصيير إلى منتهى الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings worshippers together with idols, then separates the parties, who disavow one another; idols are also brought to life.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه يجمع بين من عبد غيره وبين معبوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone receives the consequence of good or evil; no manufactured deity can help, harm, avert punishment, or independently intercede with God.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن كل أحد ينال جزاء ما قدم من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping idols and fabricating claims are human acts, for which people are punished and reproached, against the Compulsionists' account of human acts.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة والافتراء فعلهم؛ لذلك عاقبهم ووبخهم به

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read kalimāt in the plural at these occurrences, including the parallel verse in Ghāfir; other readers use singular kalimat.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر: كذلك حقت كلمات ربك على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq is an ongoing gift or benefit its recipient may use and others may not withhold; only God is called the Provider because He creates provision, like the exclusive title Lord despite ordinary possessive uses.
rows.anchor: الرزق في اللغة: هو العطاء الجاري، ومنه: رزق السلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaqqat means became obligatory; the questions press listeners to acknowledge that answer.
rows.anchor: وحقت: وجبت يقال: حققت عليك القضاء حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions establish God's unity and resurrection: God sends rain and produces plants, or sends clouds, rain, celestial bodies, and vegetation, as al-Aṣamm explains.
rows.anchor: ثم قرر تعالى عليهم أدلة التوحيد والبعث

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: God owns hearing and sight by creating and arranging these faculties, granting or taking them away, or enabling people to hear admonition and see lessons.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من يملك السمع فيسمعها المواعظ، والأبصار فيريها العظات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing the living from the dead may mean a human from a drop and a drop from a human, or giving and taking life; God's management includes day and night, seasons, people, life, and death.
rows.anchor: قيل: النطفة من الإنسان والإنسان من النطفة، وقيل: من يحييكم إذا كنتم أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists will acknowledge that God performs these acts, so they should fear His punishment and worship no other.
rows.anchor: فسيقولون الله يعني: هو الله تعالى يفعل هذه الأشياء، فقل لهم أفلا تتقون عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator of these things is the true Lord and alone deserves worship; no third rank lies between truth and error, so anything besides divine unity is false.
rows.anchor: فذلكم الله يعني فاعل هذه الأشياء ربكم خالقكم الحق أي: يحق له العبادة وحده

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: ‘Where are you being turned?’ means ‘where are you going and straying?’ even if nobody literally turns them away.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: معناه أين تذهبون وتضلون، وإن لم يكن هناك غيرهم يصرفهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The confirmed word is the sentence of punishment, threat, or judgment against those who leave faith; it may mean ‘because they do not believe.’
rows.anchor: كلمة العذاب، وقيل: كلمة الوعيد، وقيل: حكمه على الذين فسقوا

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: One interpretation says the verse foretells that people sealed in their nature will never believe; Abu ʿAli also reads it as a true report that they will not believe.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو إخبار عنهم أنهم لا يؤمنون أبدا، وهو حق وصدق لأهل الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repays their deeds without diminution; the passage censures pursuit of worldly gain and treats that pursuit and action as human acts.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على أنه تعالى يوفيهم أعمالهم من غير بخس.

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Three accounts of moral nullification are reported: between reward and punishment (Abu Hashim), between deeds (the Ikhshidiyya), or between deeds and recompense (Abu ʿAli); the author prefers the first and says the Qur'an establishes nullification.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فيه على ثلاثة [أوجه]: قيل: يقع بين الثواب والعقاب، عن أبي هاشم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina is a decisive proof separating truth from falsehood; the root conveys separation that makes something apparent.
rows.anchor: البينة: الحجة الفاصلة بين الحق والباطل، ومنه: البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥizb is a group; taḥazzaba means splitting into factions. ʿArḍ is displaying something so it can be seen and assessed.
rows.anchor: والحزب: الجماعة، وتحزب القوم إذا صاروا أحزابا وفرقا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The common reading is ḏal with zāy in ‘lying blood’; ʿĀʾisha's reading uses dāl and means fresh blood.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: بدم كذب بالذال معجمة من فوق، وعن عائشة: بدم [كدب] بالدال

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: The nominative fa-ṣabrun jamīl presumes ‘my patience’ or ‘my way’ as subject; Qutrub reports the implied-noun parsing.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة: فصبر جميل على تقدير: صبري صبر جميل

rows.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: He reads fa-ṣabran jamīlan as an accusative cognate expression meaning ‘I shall patiently endure’; other explanations exhort the self or prefer patience over grief.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: فصبرا جميلا على المصدر

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line exemplifies the accusative form ṣabran jamīlan used as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: ألا إنما مي فصبرا بلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line beginning ‘my camel complains’ witnesses ṣabrun jamīl as a nominative sentence, meaning beautiful patience is preferable to complaint.
rows.anchor: فأما الرفع فقال الشاعر: يشكوا إلي جملي طول السرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAshāʾ may mean the day's end, first darkness, a broad period from noon to morning, or time from sunset prayer to night; with fatḥa it means food.
rows.anchor: العشاء: آخر النهار، وهو طرف من أطراف الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istibāq is racing to get ahead; the text surveys race stakes and reports that foot races and wrestling may be allowed, with disagreement over compensation and whether a contract binds.
rows.anchor: يجوز بعوض وغير عوض، ولأصحاب الشافعي فيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns against diverting God's blessings into disobedience and neglecting gratitude; worldly enjoyment ending in eternal fire is blameworthy, while contentment with little that leads to Paradise is praised.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن المتمتع بالدنيا على وجه يعقب نار الأبد مذموم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read ʿibādī with a silent yāʾ; other readers vocalize it with fatḥa to resolve adjacent silent letters.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: لعبادي بإسكان الياء

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وسلام وزيد عن يعقوب
rows.claim: The common reading annexes ‘from all that you asked’; these readers put tanwīn on kull, allowing the sense that God gave unrequested things or gave each kind in the amount requested.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك وسلام وزيد عن يعقوب: من كل بالتنوين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: With tanwīn, al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God gave things people neither asked for nor imagined.
rows.anchor: فأما الحجة فقال الضحاك: أي أعطاكم أشياء ما سألتموها

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Another view says God gave all that was asked; alternatively He first bestowed gifts without being asked and also granted requested blessings.
rows.anchor: وقيل في (آتاكم) على هذه القراءة يحتمل وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāl means friendship; it can be the plural of khulla or a verbal noun for reciprocal friendship, as illustrated by Imruʾ al-Qays. Taskhīr is making something compliant and ready to serve a need.
rows.anchor: والتسخير: التذليل، وهو أن تجعل الشيء مهيأ لما تحتاج إليه

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses khilāl to mean friendship, illustrating either the plural or verbal-noun analysis.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: صرفت الهوى عنهن من خشية الردى
